# Adopt fonts / background / heading style from memani1.github.io

## Context
The user likes the typography, background color, and heading formatting on
https://memani1.github.io/ and wants their own site (a Quarto academic site)
to adopt that look. I inspected the reference site's inline `<style>` block
directly (curl) and extracted its design tokens:

- Fonts: **DM Serif Display** (headings) + **DM Sans** (body), loaded from
  Google Fonts.
- Background: warm off-white `#f7f5f0` (page bg), `#ffffff` (card/surface),
  `#f0ede6` (secondary surface).
- Ink/text colors: `#1a1714` (primary), `#4a4540` (secondary), `#7a726a`
  (tertiary/muted) — headings and body text are dark warm-grays, NOT the
  bright blue currently used for headings on this site.
- Accent: `#c0392b` (rust/brick red) used sparingly for eyebrow labels and
  hover states; `#2c5f8a` (muted blue) used for links.
- Heading treatment: serif font, tight line-height (1.08–1.2), slightly
  negative letter-spacing on large display headings, no heavy borders.

This site's current styling lives in `styles/custom.scss` (3,982 lines,
Quarto/Bootstrap SCSS theme) with variables from `styles/_variables.scss`.
Key facts found during exploration:
- `_quarto.yml` loads theme as `[flatly, styles/custom.scss]`.
- `custom.scss` line 4 imports `_variables.scss`, then **redeclares**
  `$font-family-sans-serif` / `$font-family-serif` (lines 7–8) — these
  redeclarations win, so only `custom.scss` needs editing for fonts.
- Current font import/vars: Neuton (serif) + IBM Plex Sans (sans), line 7-13.
- Color tokens are CSS custom properties under `:root` (lines 16-29) and a
  dark-mode override block `[data-bs-theme="dark"]` (lines 162-167+).
- Headings are globally styled at lines 462-547: forced serif font, forced
  `color: var(--global-theme-color)` (currently Swiss blue `#0066cc`),
  per-level font sizes or weights, and `h2` has a `border-bottom`.
- Body text/base color: `--global-text-color: #{$black-color}` (line 19),
  applied via a broad selector at lines 443-446 and 471-477.

## Approach
Edit `styles/custom.scss` only — swap fonts, background/surface/text tokens,
and heading color/weight/spacing to mirror the reference site, while keeping
this site's existing structure, layout, and dark-mode toggle intact (dark
mode gets its own analogous warm-dark tokens rather than being deleted).

### 1. Fonts (lines 6-13)
- Replace the Google Fonts `@import` with DM Serif Display + DM Sans:
  `family=DM+Serif+Display:ital@0;1&family=DM+Sans:ital,opsz,wght@0,9..40,300;0,9..40,400;0,9..40,500;1,9..40,300`
- Set `$font-family-serif: "DM Serif Display", Georgia, serif;`
- Set `$font-family-sans-serif: "DM Sans", system-ui, sans-serif;`

### 2. Color tokens — light mode (lines 16-29)
- `--global-bg-color`: `#f7f5f0` (was white)
- `--global-card-bg-color`: `#ffffff` (surface, unchanged effectively)
- `--global-text-color`: `#1a1714` (was pure black)
- `--global-text-color-light`: `#7a726a` (muted ink, was mid-grey)
- `--global-theme-color`: `#2c5f8a` (muted blue for links — replaces Swiss
  blue `#0066cc`; keeps a link-like feel rather than making everything rust)
- `--global-divider-color`: `#ddd8ce` (warm border, was rgba black)
- Add nothing structurally new — reuse existing var names so every other
  rule in the file that already consumes these vars picks up the new look
  for free.

### 3. Color tokens — dark mode (`[data-bs-theme="dark"]` block, ~line 162)
- Give it an analogous warm-dark palette instead of the current neutral
  grey-dark, so dark mode doesn't clash: bg `#1a1714`, text `#f0ede6`,
  accent `#5b9bd5` (lighter muted blue for contrast). Kept minimal — only
  adjust the same variable names already declared there.

### 4. Heading rules (lines 462-547)
- Change the forced heading `color` from `var(--global-theme-color)` to
  `var(--global-text-color)` (ink, not blue/link-color) — matches
  reference's h2 using ink, not accent.
- Adjust `font-weight` on headings toward 400 (DM Serif Display is a
  display serif, doesn't need heavy weight), `line-height: 1.15-1.2`.
- Remove the `h2` `border-bottom` (lines 507-508) for the cleaner,
  border-free heading look from the reference.
- Keep the existing responsive size breakpoints (991px/575px) as-is —
  just carried through with new color/weight/line-height.

## Files to change
- `styles/custom.scss` — only file touched (fonts, `:root` color tokens,
  dark-mode tokens, heading rules).

## Verification
1. `quarto render index.qmd` (and `quarto render` for the full site) to
   confirm no SCSS/build errors.
2. Visually check `_site/index.html`, `_site/cv.html`, and a blog post in a
   browser (or via `open _site/index.html`) to confirm:
   - Body renders in DM Sans, headings in DM Serif Display.
   - Background is warm off-white, not stark white.
   - Headings read in dark ink, not blue, with no border under h2.
   - Dark mode toggle still works and looks coherent (warm dark bg).
3. Spot-check that links/hover states still have visible contrast against
   the new background.

<tool-use data-tool-type="generic" data-tool-name="AskUserQuestion"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **AskUserQuestion**</summary>
**custom.scss has ~230 animation/transition rules — page-load fade-ins, staggered list/table entrances, floating icons, background gradient shifts, pulsing badges, plus a lot of dead rules for things this site doesn't have (carousels, chat bubbles, pricing tables, modals). How far should I go?**

Options:
- **Strip to minimal (Recommended)** - Remove all entrance/decorative animations (fade-in, slide-in, float, pulse, spin, background shift, staggered delays). Keep only simple, fast hover color/opacity transitions on links and buttons for basic feedback.
- **Tone down, don't remove** - Keep all animations but cut durations/delays substantially (e.g. 0.6s→0.2s) and drop staggering, so things still animate but much more subtly and quickly.
- **Disable everything** - Set animation:none and transition:none globally — a fully static site with zero motion, including hover states.


**Answer:** Strip to minimal (Recommended)
</details></tool-use>

```bash
cd "/Users/frimpsjoe/Documents/frimpsjoek.github.io" && cp styles/custom.scss /tmp/custom.scss.bak && python3 << 'EOF'
import re

with open("styles/custom.scss") as f:
    text = f.read()

lines = text.split("\n")
out = []
i = 0
removed_keyframes = []
n = len(lines)
while i < n:
    line = lines[i]
    m = re.match(r'\s*@keyframes\s+([\w-]+)\s*\{', line)
    if m:
        # find matching closing brace by tracking depth
        depth = line.count('{') - line.count('}')
        removed_keyframes.append(m.group(1))
        i += 1
        while i < n and depth > 0:
            depth += lines[i].count('{') - lines[i].count('}')
            i += 1
        continue
    out.append(line)
    i += 1

text2 = "\n".join(out)

# Now remove animation declarations (but keep explicit "animation: none" disabling lines)
lines = text2.split("\n")
out2 = []
removed_lines = 0
for line in lines:
    stripped = line.strip()
    if re.match(r'^animation(-delay|-duration|-name|-fill-mode|-iteration-count)?\s*:', stripped):
        if re.match(r'^animation\s*:\s*none\b', stripped):
            out2.append(line)
        else:
            removed_lines += 1
            continue
    else:
        out2.append(line)

text3 = "\n".join(out2)

with open("styles/custom.scss", "w") as f:
    f.write(text3)

print("Removed keyframes:", len(removed_keyframes))
print(removed_keyframes)
print("Removed animation declaration lines:", removed_lines)
EOF
```

I've opened `index.html` and `projects.html` — take a look. Summary of what changed in `styles/custom.scss`:

- **Removed 32 `@keyframes` blocks** and every associated `animation:`/`animation-delay:` declaration — page-load fade-ins, staggered list/table/timeline entrances, floating icons, spinning, pulsing, background-color cycling, and the SPA-style page-transition classes.

- **Cleaned up orphaned empty rule blocks** left behind by the removals.
- Left alone a handful of transform-hover rules that only target unused markup (chat bubbles, pricing tables, testimonial carousels, etc. — confirmed via grep that no `.qmd` file uses those classes), since they never render and touching them adds no visible benefit.

The site still renders cleanly across all 28 pages and brace-balance checks out. Everything is unstaged — let me know if you want it committed, or if any particular hover/transition still feels like too much motion.

32	I am postdoctoral researcher at Argonne National Laboratory, where I study the electronic structure and optical properties of materials to advance applications in catalysis, energy, and optoelectronics. My research focuses on computational methods, including density functional theory (DFT), many-body perturbation theory (GW/BSE), and machine learning, to explore structure-property relationships in heterogeneous interfaces, quantum dots, and other nanoscale materials. I am also passionate about leveraging computational chemistry and machine learning to accelerate materials discovery and improve the efficiency of next-generation materials.
